solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tom couldn't do this flip

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, which cannot give birth to a litter; the phrase for that also means to flip, lose one's cool

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom fails to manage a somersault or a flip of a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' reads as a man's name, but it is a male cat. 'Flip' is the everyday sense: to panic or get very agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to become extremely anxious or upset, while literally it is giving birth to young cats, which a male cat cannot do.

clue.text: Produce changing hands, split equally with good man

indicators.note: the left hand swaps for the right, so the L abbreviation becomes R in the word

parts.note: to split something equally is to halve it
ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: Goods change hands in a deal shared fifty-fifty with a decent fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' swaps L (left) for R (right) in HALVE, giving HARVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the crop gathered in, which is farm produce.

clue.text: Brought up daughter with mostly simplistic food

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
most of the word is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: naive means simplistic, unsophisticated

explanation.surface: A girl raised on a diet of overly plain food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims NAIVE to NAIV; D plus NAIV is DNAIV, and 'Brought up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Viand is an old word for an item of food, usually in the plural for provisions.

clue.text: Heartlessly whip around school being ostentatious

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes round the school abbreviation
without its heart, the centre letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a whip-round is a collection, and a kitty is the pooled money

explanation.surface: A cruel flogging around a school turns into a showy display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' is not a lash but a whip-round, the pooled cash; 'Heartlessly' leaves KITY, and 'around' wraps it round the school.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitschy describes showy, tasteless decoration, which is a garish, ostentatious style.

clue.text: Vehicle guarded by explosive weapon

indicators.note: the vehicle word is protected on both sides by the explosive's letters

parts.note: TNT is the familiar explosive
a ride is a vehicle in the sense of a car or lift someone gives you

explanation.surface: An armoured car protected by explosives is itself a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-pronged spear is a weapon; it is also the name of Britain's nuclear missile system.

clue.text: Moving to Lima, one is at sea

indicators.note: being at sea is being confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone sails off to Lima, and one of the party is adrift on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like travel to Lima, but it is the definition, in its sense of stirring the feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving film or speech is one that stirs the feelings, which is an emotional one.

clue.text: Son supplies European officer to set up one of several targets

parts.note: kit is equipment, supplies

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: LT is short for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A boy gives a European officer the gear needed to set up a range of targets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To set up' reverses E plus LT to give TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game of ninepins, each of the pins knocked down by the bowled ball is a target among several.

clue.text: Please show anger over male being inactive

parts.note: do serves as please in a request such as do come in

indicators.note: the angry word goes over, covering, the male letter

parts.note: to rant is to show anger noisily

explanation.surface: A plea to vent fury at a man who does nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is asleep or not active for now, like a volcano that is quiet.

clue.text: Went mad to support music event university put off

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word supporting others sits below them

parts.note: a disco is an evening of dancing to recorded music
raged means went mad with anger

explanation.surface: A university frowned on a music event after people went wild.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put off from doing something is to be deterred or disheartened by it.

clue.text: Choppers soldiers hid among evergreens

indicators.note: the soldiers are concealed in the middle of the plants' letters

parts.note: ivies are evergreen climbing plants
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Helicopters with troops hidden among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choppers' suggests helicopters, but it is slang for teeth, matching the old use of ivory for teeth and piano keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivories is slang for teeth, and choppers is equally informal for the same set of biters.

clue.text: In Scottish island, plant density shot up

indicators.note: the plant word goes in the island's name

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides
rocket is a salad plant, also called arugula
D is the symbol for density in physics

explanation.surface: On a Scottish island, thick vegetation grew rapidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the plant going inside the island, and density's symbol follows the island's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that skyrocketed rose very fast, like something that has shot up.

clue.text: Mount Everest's old rocks — no place for new lovers

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes, so these letters are jumbled
the jumbled letters of the other word have no place, so they are taken out

explanation.surface: Everest's ancient rocks are no spot for honeymooners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' jumbles EVERESTSOLD; 'no place for new lovers' takes out the letters of LOVERS in any order, leaving E, E, T, S, D to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is a horse for riding, and a steed is a horse, especially a spirited one.

clue.text: Around quarter of the world, perhaps, aim to establish rapport

parts.note: C, circa, means around, approximately
a hemisphere is half of the world, so the first half of that word playfully gives a quarter of it
to aim to do something is to try to do it

explanation.surface: Someone aims to build a rapport across a quarter of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: HEMIS is half of HEMISPHERE, itself half the world, so a quarter of the world; 'perhaps' flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry between people is a natural mutual attraction or understanding, the same idea as a good rapport.

clue.text: Best piano secured by payment

indicators.note: the musical letter is held fast inside the payment word

parts.note: an outlay is an amount spent, a payment
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: The finest piano is obtained with a payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat them, and to outplay them is to perform better than them.

clue.text: See mud-slinging expose husband as boaster

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold

indicators.note: slinging means throwing about, so these letters are flung into a new order

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them publicly

explanation.surface: Watch the smear campaign show up a husband as a braggart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slinging' turns MUD into UDM.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudmouth talks too much and too noisily, often bragging, like a boaster.

clue.text: Messenger on time with old cross

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: angel comes from the Greek for messenger

explanation.surface: A courier arrives punctually with an old bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry; it is a noun, a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: This fruit is a hybrid of a tangerine and a pomelo or grapefruit, so a cross between citrus varieties.

clue.text: Monarch repulsed by peer is to run off

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch
a count is a nobleman, a peer

explanation.surface: A queen, rebuffed by a nobleman, is about to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run off' reads as fleeing, but it means to reel off or recite.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount events is to narrate them in order, which is what to reel off or list them means.

clue.text: Generally, after losing millions, toll's put on career

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece is placed on top of the second
once the millions abbreviation is lost the word is shorter

parts.note: a toll of a bell is its chime
to career is to rush along, to fly

explanation.surface: In general, once millions are gone, a fee is imposed on someone's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toll' and 'career' look financial and professional; they are a bell's ring and a verb for speeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiefly means mainly or for the most part, which is what generally means.

clue.text: Composition switched after radius is found in upper arm

indicators.note: the turned composition comes after the other piece
the radius letter sits inside the upper word

parts.note: top as an adjective means upper

indicators.note: switched means turned round, so the poem's letters run backwards

parts.note: an ode is a poetic composition

explanation.surface: An essay rearranged once a bone of the forearm is found in the upper limb.
explanation.walkthrough: The radius is a forearm bone, which makes 'upper arm' read as anatomy; 'arm' alone is the weapon. 'Switched' gives EDO, and 'is found in' gives TORP.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, and a self-propelled underwater missile is one such weapon.

clue.text: Swimmer's to cut around section of waterway

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the cutting word reads backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off branches
a lock is a gated section of a canal or river

explanation.surface: A swimmer is about to cut round part of a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Swimmer', with the 's as a link meaning is; 'around' turns the cutting word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fish of the cod family, and a fish is a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Hawks speed around swallows and owl in the end

indicators.note: the jumbled word takes the end letters inside itself
around means moved about, so the letters of speed are mixed up
only the closing letter of each of those two words is used

explanation.surface: Birds of prey speed about, swallowing an owl at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' rearranges SPEED to PEDES; 'in the end' takes D and L from 'and' and 'owl', which PEDES swallows.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to sell them in the street, and to peddle them means the same.

clue.text: Troublesome leg to move, after foot's fully raised

parts.note: on is the leg side of a cricket field

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the bottom letter, which is lifted right to the top

parts.note: to rouse is to stir, move into action

explanation.surface: A bad leg will move only after the foot is lifted high.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also the on side, so ON. The final E of ROUSE, its foot in a down light, goes to the top for EROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is a heavy burden, which is a troublesome thing to deal with.

clue.text: Grand lake covered in mild rippling twinkled

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: the lake word is wrapped inside the rearranged letters
rippling suggests disturbance, so the letters are churned up

parts.note: a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: A great lake, softly rippling, sparkled in the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rippling' gives LIMD, and 'covered in' wraps that round the lake: LIM-MERE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Glimmered means shone faintly and unsteadily, much as a star that twinkled did.

clue.text: Grouse caught in noble attempt

indicators.note: the letters are trapped inside these two words, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: A game bird shot during a grand attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb, to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to grumble, and to bleat is to complain in a feeble, whining way.

clue.text: Educated person, so crude

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: An educated person who is nonetheless coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crude is simple and unrefined, rudimentary, which is the sense of basic here.

clue.text: Broadcast majority of conflict around America

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the country abbreviation
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: views that conflict differ

explanation.surface: Transmit most of the war going on around the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conflict' is a verb here, as views conflict; 'majority of' leaves DIFFE, and 'around' sets it round the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To diffuse news is to spread it widely, the same as to broadcast it.

clue.text: Article in French vessel with great volume is caught

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article
SS, steamship, is a vessel
the OED, the Oxford English Dictionary, is a famously huge book

explanation.surface: A French item aboard a ship with a huge book is seized.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer that is lassoed has been roped and caught with a noosed line.

clue.text: Boss you hack off produces exclamation of contempt

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Your boss annoys you, and you fire back a jeer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack off' reads as annoy, but 'hack' is fodder and 'off' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This childish taunt is a playground jeer, used to sneer at someone's misfortune.
